sources.title: Associates Program Operating Agreement
sources.establishes: The required affiliate disclosure statement, and the requirement that it appear clearly and prominently on the Site.
sources.quote: You must clearly and prominently state the following, or any substantially similar statement previously allowed under this Agreement, on your Site or any other location where Amazon may authorize your display or other use of Program Content: “As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.”

sources.title: Associates Program Policies (Commission Income Statement, Participation Requirements, Products Statement, Mobile Application Policy, Trademark Guidelines, IP License)
sources.establishes: Link formatting (tag parameter), direct-access rule, price-display conditions, star-rating prohibition, link-shortener clarity rule, price-tracking prohibition, cookie disclosure duty, and the Redirecting Link disqualification.
sources.quote: You must not encourage customers to bookmark your Special Links. All Special Links must be accessed directly from your Site.

sources.title: Standard Commission Income rate card
sources.establishes: NOTHING. This URL redirects to an Associates sign-in page. Commission rates are therefore unverified and no rate, earnings estimate or revenue forecast may be published.

sources.title: FTC's Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking
sources.section: “Where in my blog should I disclose that my review is sponsored by a marketer?”
sources.establishes: Placement standard for affiliate disclosures, and that the FTC does not mandate specific disclosure wording.
sources.quote: A disclosure should be placed where it easily catches consumers’ attention and is difficult to miss. … Consumers may miss a disclosure at the bottom of a blog or page. … A disclosure is more likely to be seen if it’s very close to, or – even better – part of, the endorsement to which it relates.

sources.title: 16 CFR Part 255 — Guides Concerning Use of Endorsements and Testimonials in Advertising
sources.publisher: U.S. Federal Trade Commission (via eCFR, National Archives)
sources.updated_on_page: eCFR up to date as of 11/18/2026; source 88 FR 48102 (Jul 26, 2023)
sources.establishes: The operative rule text requiring disclosure of material connections, of which §255.5 is the section on point for affiliate relationships.

sources.title: Understanding ASINs: Your guide to Amazon's product identification system
sources.publisher: Amazon (Sell on Amazon, official seller blog)
sources.section: What does “ASIN” mean? / How to find and use ASIN numbers
sources.establishes: Official definition of ASIN and its 10-character length, and that the ASIN appears in a product URL after "/dp/".
sources.quote: “ASIN” stands for “Amazon Standard Identification Number.” It’s a unique 10-character alphanumeric code assigned to every product listed in the Amazon store.
